7. Track `max_turns` and watch every in-flight task from GitHub and history, never from panes, at the orchestrator's own action boundaries and at least every 30 minutes after a TASK: list the PR's commits, the Bot's reviews, its top-level review comments and the check runs (`gh api --paginate repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<n>/commits`, `…/reviews`, `…/pulls/<n>/comments`, all three with `--paginate`, and `gh pr checks <n>`; once A3 is on `main`, `scripts/regime-counters.sh <task id> --pr <n>` gives the same counts in one line) and the task's PONGs in history, so an INV-6 head count crossed by a worker that ignores its PING is seen from the inline P0/P1 threads. The cadence mechanism is one bounded background wait of at most 30 minutes per task between reads, never a foreground sleep loop; the watch reads state and never detects completion, which stays the RESULT's arrival through the Monitor or turn delivery. 45 minutes without a push, a PONG or a RESULT is a stall: send `AGMSG-PING v1` and wait one turn. The watch also sends `AGMSG-PING v1` as soon as it first sees a task past the A2 cap or an INV-6 count, without waiting for a stall. When pushes continue past the A2 cap or an INV-6 count after the PING, read or unread, the orchestrator removes the seat with `herdr-agents --remove-worker <worktree> --force`; the stopped worktree's evidence is preserved and the next seat is created in a clean worktree; the acceptance record names the PING id and the stop.
